problem.paragraph: Given points $$\textbf{p}_{1} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}$$ , $$\textbf{p}_{2} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}$$ , and $$\textbf{p}_{3} = \left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} {- 1} \\ 2 \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ in $$\mathbb{R}^{2}$$ , let $$S = \text{conv} \left\{ \textbf{p}_{1},\textbf{p}_{2},\textbf{p}_{3} \right\}$$ . For each linear functional $$f$$ , find the maximum value $$m$$ of $$f$$ on the set $$S$$ , and find all points $$\textbf{x}$$ in $$S$$ at which $$f\left( \textbf{x} \right) = m$$ .﻿

list.item: $$f \left(\right. x_{1} , x_{2} \left.\right) = x_{1} - x_{2}$$
$$f \left(\right. x_{1} , x_{2} \left.\right) = x_{1} + x_{2}$$
$$f \left(\right. x_{1} , x_{2} \left.\right) = - 3 x_{1} + x_{2}$$

problem.paragraph: Given points $$\textbf{p}_{1} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ {- 1} \end{bmatrix}$$ , $$\textbf{p}_{2} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$$ , and $$\textbf{p}_{3} = \left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} 1 \\ 2 \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ in $$\mathbb{R}^{2}$$ , let $$S = \text{conv} \left\{ \textbf{p}_{1},\textbf{p}_{2},\textbf{p}_{3} \right\}$$ . For each linear functional $$f$$ , find the maximum value $$m$$ of $$f$$ on the set $$S$$ , and find all points $$\textbf{x}$$ in $$S$$ at which $$f\left( \textbf{x} \right) = m$$ .﻿

list.item: $$f \left(\right. x_{1} , x_{2} \left.\right) = x_{1} + x_{2}$$
$$f \left(\right. x_{1} , x_{2} \left.\right) = x_{1} - x_{2}$$
$$f \left(\right. x_{1} , x_{2} \left.\right) = - 2 x_{1} + x_{2}$$

problem.paragraph: Repeat Exercise 1 where $$m$$ is the minimum value of $$f$$ on $$S$$ instead of the maximum value.
Repeat Exercise 2 where $$m$$ is the minimum value of $$f$$ on $$S$$ instead of the maximum value.

exercise_group.instruction: In Exercises 5–8, find the minimal representation of the polytope defined by the inequalities $$A\textbf{x} \leq \textbf{b}$$ and $$\textbf{x} \geq \textbf{0}$$ ﻿.

problem.paragraph: $$A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$$ , $$\textbf{b} = \begin{bmatrix} 10 \\ 15 \end{bmatrix}$$
$$A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$$ , $$\textbf{b} = \begin{bmatrix} 18 \\ 16 \end{bmatrix}$$
$$A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 4 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$$ , $$\textbf{b} = \begin{bmatrix} 18 \\ 10 \\ 28 \end{bmatrix}$$
$$A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$$ , $$\textbf{b} = \begin{bmatrix} 8 \\ 6 \\ 7 \end{bmatrix}$$
Let $$S = \left\{ (x,y):x^{2} + (y - 1)^{2} \leq 1 \right\} \cup \left\{ (3,0) \right\}$$ . Is the origin an extreme point of $$\text{conv} S$$ ? Is the origin a vertex of $$\text{conv} S$$ ?
Find an example of a closed convex set $$S$$ in $$\mathbb{R}^{2}$$ such that its profile $$P$$ is nonempty but $$\text{conv} P \neq S$$ .﻿
Find an example of a bounded convex set $$S$$ in $$\mathbb{R}^{2}$$ such that its profile $$P$$ is nonempty but $$\text{conv} P \neq S$$ .﻿

list.item: Determine the number of $$k$$ -faces of the $$\text{5-dimensional}$$ simplex $$S^{5}$$ for $$k = 0,1,\ldots,4$$ . Verify that your answer satisfies Euler’s formula.
Make a chart of the values of $$f_{k}(S^{n})$$ for $$n = 1,\ldots,5$$ and $$k = 0,1,\ldots,4$$ . Can you see a pattern? Guess a general formula for $$f_{k}\left( S^{n} \right)$$ .﻿
Determine the number of $$k \text{-faces}$$ of the $$\text{5-dimensional}$$ hypercube $$C^{5}$$ for $$k = 0,1,\ldots,4$$ . Verify that your answer satisfies Euler’s formula.
Make a chart of the values of $$f_{k}(C^{n})$$ for $$n = 1,\ldots,5$$ and $$k = 0,1,\ldots,4$$ . Can you see a pattern? Guess a general formula for $$f_{k}\left( C^{n} \right)$$ .﻿

problem.paragraph: Suppose $$\textbf{v}_{1},\ldots,\textbf{v}_{k}$$ are linearly independent vectors in $$\mathbb{R}^{n}(1 \leq k \leq n)$$ . Then the set $$X^{k} = \text{conv \{} \pm \textbf{v}_{1},\ldots, \pm \textbf{v}_{k} \text{\}}$$ is called a k-crosspolytope.

list.item: Determine the number of $$k$$ $$\text{-faces}$$ of the $$\text{3-dimensional}$$ crosspolytope $$X^{3}$$ for $$k = 0,1,2$$ . What is another name for $$X^{3}$$ ?
Determine the number of $$k \text{-faces}$$ of the $$\text{4-dimensional}$$ crosspolytope $$X^{4}$$ for $$k = 0,1,2,3$$ . Verify that your answer satisfies Euler’s formula.
Find a formula for $$f_{k}\left( X^{n} \right)$$ , the number of $$k \text{-faces}$$ of $$X^{n}$$ , for $$0 \leq k \leq n - 1$$ .﻿

problem.paragraph: A $$\mathbf{\mathit{k}} -\textbf{pyramid}$$ $$P^{k}$$ is the convex hull of a $$\left(\right. k - 1 \left.\right) - \text{polytope}$$ $$Q$$ and a point $$\mathbf{x} \notin \text{aff} Q$$ . Find a formula for each of the following in terms of $$f_{j}(Q)$$ , $$j = 0,\ldots,n - 1$$ .﻿

list.item: The number of vertices of $$P^{n}$$ : $$f_{0}\left( P^{n} \right)$$ .﻿
The number of $$k$$ -faces of $$P^{n}$$ : $$f_{k}\left( P^{n} \right)$$ , for $$1 \leq k \leq n - 2$$ .﻿
The number of $$\left( n - 1 \text{)-dimensional} \right.$$ facets of $$P^{n}$$ : $$f_{n - 1}\left( P^{n} \right)$$ .﻿

exercise_group.instruction: In Exercises 16–23, mark each statement True or False (T/F). Justify each answer.

problem.paragraph: (T/F) A polytope is the convex hull of a finite set of points.
(T/F) A cube in $$\mathbb{R}^{3}$$ has exactly five facets.

(T/F) Let $$\textbf{p}$$ be an extreme point of a convex set $$S$$ . If $$\textbf{u}$$ , $$\textbf{v} \in S$$ , $$\textbf{p} \in \overset{‾}{\textbf{uv}}$$ , and $$\textbf{p} \neq \textbf{u}$$ , then $$\textbf{p} = \textbf{v}$$ .﻿
(T/F) A point $$\textbf{p}$$ is an extreme point of a polytope $$P$$ if and only if $$\textbf{p}$$ is a vertex of $$P$$ .﻿
(T/F) If $$S$$ is a nonempty convex subset of $$\mathbb{R}^{n}$$ , then $$S$$ is the convex hull of its profile.
(T/F) If $$S$$ is a nonempty compact convex set and a linear functional attains its maximum at a point $$\textbf{p}$$ , then $$\textbf{p}$$ is an extreme point of $$S$$ .﻿
(T/F) The $$\text{4-dimensional}$$ simplex $$S^{4}$$ has exactly five facets, each of which is a $$\text{3-dimensional}$$ tetrahedron.
(T/F) A $$\text{2-dimensional}$$ polytope always has the same number of vertices and edges.
Let $$\textbf{v}$$ be an element of the convex set $$S$$ . Prove that $$\textbf{v}$$ is an extreme point of $$S$$ if and only if the set $$\{\textbf{x} \in S:\textbf{x} \neq \textbf{v}\}$$ is convex.

If $$c \in \mathbb{R}$$ and $$S$$ is a set, define $$cS = \left\{ c\textbf{x}:\textbf{x} \in S \right\}$$ . Let $$S$$ be a convex set and suppose $$c > 0$$ and $$d > 0$$ . Prove that $$cS + dS = (c + d)S$$ .﻿
Find an example to show that the convexity of $$S$$ is necessary in Exercise 25.
If $$A$$ and $$B$$ are convex sets, prove that $$A + B$$ is convex.

A polyhedron $$\text{(3-polytope)}$$ is called regular if all its facets are congruent regular polygons and all the angles at the vertices are equal. Supply the details in the following proof that there are only five regular polyhedra.

list.item: Suppose that a regular polyhedron has $$r$$ facets, each of which is a $$k$$ -sided regular polygon, and that $$s$$ edges meet at each vertex. Letting $$v$$ and $$e$$ denote the numbers of vertices and edges in the polyhedron, explain why $$kr = 2e$$ and $$sv = 2e$$ .﻿
Use Euler’s formula to show that $$\frac{1}{s} + \frac{1}{k} = \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{e}$$ .﻿
Find all the integral solutions of the equation in part (b) that satisfy the geometric constraints of the problem. (How small can $$k$$ and $$s$$ be?)

problem.paragraph: For your information, the five regular polyhedra are the tetrahedron $$(4, 6, 4)$$ , the cube $$(8, 12, 6)$$ , the octahedron $$(6, 12, 8)$$ , the dodecahedron $$(20, 30, 12)$$ , and the icosahedron $$(12, 30, 20)$$ . (The numbers in parentheses indicate the numbers of vertices, edges, and faces, respectively.)
